question: By whom was the equation C = KPgₐₛ formulated in 1803?
solution:
The correct answer is __**William Henry.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** C = KPgₐₛ**

 
 
• **​The equation C = KPgₐₛ, also known as Henry's Law, was formulated by William Henry, an English chemist and physician, in 1803.**
 
• This law states that the amount of a gas that dissolves in a given type and volume of liquid is directly proportional to the partial pressure of that gas in equilibrium with that liquid.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Edme Mariotte:-**

 
 
• **He was a French physicist and priest who is best known for his work on the relationship between the pressure and volume of gases. **
 
• In 1679, he published a paper in which he stated that the pressure of a gas is inversely proportional to its volume at a constant temperature.
 
• This is known as Boyle's Law, after Robert Boyle, who had independently discovered the same relationship in 1662.
 
 
 
• **Jacques Charles:-**
 
 
• **He was a French physicist and mathematician who is best known for his work on the relationship between the volume and temperature of gases. **
 
• In 1787, he published a paper in which he stated that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to its temperature at a constant pressure. This is known as Charles's Law.
 
 
 
• **Robert Boyle:-**
 
 
• **He was an English natural philosopher, chemist, physicist, inventor, alchemist, and theologian. **
 
• Boyle is best known for his formulation of the Boyle–Mariotte law, an experimental relationship between the volume and pressure of a gas at a constant temperature.
 
• His work in chemistry included the discovery of hydrogen and the formulation of the gas laws. He is regarded as one of the founders of modern chemistry.
